Executive Order,

Wuernas, The Urgent Deficiency Bill H. R. 9867, approved March 28,
rgtS, aathorizes the Commissioners of the District of Columbia to construct
24 inch water mains along certain streets, to wit +-
“For constructing twenty-four-inch water rains in ‘Twenty-first Street,
fron L Street to Virginia Avenue; in Virginia Avenue to New York Avenue;
j in New York Avenue between Virginia Avenue and Nineteenth and I
Streets; iu 1) Street between Seventeenth and Nineteenth Streets; and in
Seventeenth Street between [Street and New York Avenue, $70,000, to
contince available during the fiseal year nineteeu hundred and nineteen.
For construeting twenty-four-inch water main in ‘Twenty-first Street
} frou Virginia Avene to B Street, and in B Street hetween Seventeenth
and Twenty-first Streets, $39,000; and for constructing sixteen-ineh water
main in B Street between Twenty-first and Twenty-sixth Streets and in
. Twenty-sixth Street between LB and D Streets, $18,700; and for construct-
ing a twenty-ineh water main in Missouri Avenue between Four-and-a-half
j and Sixth Streets Northwest, $6,000; and for constructing twelve-inch
water main in the Mall between Seventh and Ninth Streets and B Street
north and B Street south, $2,400; in all, $66,700, to continue available ;
during the fiscal year nineteen hundred and nineteen,” :
Wherkas, These water rains are to be constructed for the convenience of
ofiice buildings erected by the United States Government in this vicinity in
connection with work relating to the present war, and
| Wuereas, The Commissioners of the District of Columbia have requested
that this be declared an evergency matter, and have asked that the Hight
] Hour Law relating to the e nployment of laborers and mechanics in the District
i of Cohurbia, be waived in connection with the construction of these water mains;
THEREFORE, Be it ordered, that 1, Wooprow Winson, President of the
United States, do hereby declare that the construction of the said water mains
is an emergency iveasure relating to the conduct of the present war, and it is
hereby excepted from the provisions of the Hight Hour Law governing the
hours of laborers and nechanies in connection therewith. ‘
PRovipeD, however, that pay be allowed to those entitled thereto in the
construction of said water mains with compensation of time and a half for over
time work spent upon said construction.
WOODROW WILSON
Tun Wurre House,
20 April, rors,
. [No. 2842,]
